title: Adapting through a long task
description: Fruit placement, recovery and vessel manipulation unfold across 66 calls; the final score is 0.6.
instruction: Make a fruit milkshake directly in the cup.
initial_prompt:
Complete this single task yourself using the tools: Make a fruit milkshake directly in the cup.
Robot: manip/lift2/R5a, two arms and a movable planar base. Left arm is left in the overlook view. EEF poses are local to each arm's planner base: +X forward, +Y robot-left, +Z up; quaternion order wxyz. Fingers extend along tool +X and open along tool Y. Wrist cameras move/rotate with the hands. Measured local EEF z is not height above the tabletop. There is no supplied depth, object pose or camera calibration. Only RGB and measured robot EEF/gripper/base state are available. Base observed yaw is radians; tool command yaw is degrees. You have one continuous conversation and may choose any continuous EEF target, both arms, base motion and waypoint batching. Use execute_eef sequentially, not parallel calls. Use observations to judge motion and object manipulation. The server determines task success independently. Do not start another episode. Resource limits: unlimited tool calls, physics deadline enforced by the server; no hard token limit; resource reminders start after 2,000,000 cumulative tokens. Resource reminders ask you to reduce unnecessary token use while continuing useful work. Select only useful camera views after the initial observation to control resource use. When finished, state the observed outcome concisely.
Manipulation guidance: after visually aligning, close at a stationary pose and allow settling. A nonzero finger gap on the table is contact evidence, not proof of a secure grasp. Test each grasp by lifting only 0.01 m first, using motion_steps=16 or more, then hold 8..16 steps and request the active wrist plus overlook views. Keep orientation and base fixed during this test. Check both finger gap and RGB to confirm the object rises with the gripper before further lifting or transport. If it remains on the table or slips, lower and adjust local contact depth/centering using current images. There is no fixed limit on failed grasp attempts; retry or change approach within the remaining experiment budgets. Avoid large instantaneous target jumps while holding an object; use motion_steps for controlled transport. Total steps per waypoint must remain <=64 and includes the ramp. Use only the active wrist for local corrections, adding overlook when establishing alignment, testing grasp, or verifying placement.
RGB inputs are downsampled: overlook 640x360, wrist 384x288; no crop or object annotation.

arguments.reason: Approach the near orange fruit with an open downward-facing hand.
Center and lower over the orange fruit.
The fingers closed above the fruit; reopen and deepen the contact.
Shift backward to center the fruit between the finger pads.
Test the fruit grasp with a one-centimeter lift.
Carry the secured fruit above the small cup, not the large jug.
Align the held fruit with the cup opening using the wrist view.
Place the fruit just above the center of the cup.
Recover the fruit that landed behind the cup.
Refine the recovery grasp.
Verify the recovered fruit rises with the hand.
Lift clear and move backward over the cup's mouth.
Approach the red fruit for direct placement into the cup.
Center the red fruit between the pads.
Test the red fruit grasp with a small controlled lift.
Transport the red fruit above the cup.
Approach the remaining small green fruit.
Center the green fruit.
Check the green fruit grasp with a one-centimeter lift.
Carry the green fruit directly over the cup.
Approach the small vessel's handle to transfer its contents into the large mixing cup.
Reopen and lower onto the vessel handle.
Align with the near handle rather than the rim.
Finish centering the handle between the fingers.
Test whether the current contact securely holds the vessel.
Lift slowly to distinguish the held fruit from the surrounding vessel.
Carry the secured vessel and fruit toward the large mixing cup.
Recover the loose red fruit beside the mixing cup.
Lower onto the red fruit resting on the mango segment.
Back away from the obstructing vessel to reassess the fruit positions.
Lower the finger pads onto the red fruit while avoiding the vessel rim.
Test the red fruit grasp before transport.
Lift clear and position the red fruit over the large cup.
Center the fruit over the large cup interior.
Approach the orange fruit still inside the small vessel.
Lower narrowly into the vessel around the orange fruit.
Test the rim grasp with a one-centimeter lift.
Raise the rim-held vessel slowly while monitoring for slip.
Move the small vessel above the large cup for pouring.
Tilt the small vessel toward the large cup interior.
Inspect the tipped vessel and recover its remaining fruit.
Grasp across the tipped vessel's body rather than its thin rim.
Seat the pads around the vessel body.
Test the wider body grasp with a small lift.
Lift and carry the securely held vessel above the large cup.
Slowly tip the body-held vessel into the large cup.
Return the emptied vessel to the table.
Return to the remaining green fruit.
Lower onto the green fruit.

alignment.method: Recorded nonterminal execution chunks in order, one video frame per returned state; frame counts checked against each encoded video. The terminal result has no additional video frame.

scope: Complete archived public tool-call sequence and initial task prompt. Response summaries are preserved; the execution video is not a reconstruction of all model input images.
